title: Stimulation-Guided AAV Delivery and Longitudinal Assessment of Optogenetic Expression in Rat Motor Nerves
author: Emma M. Moravec

steps.title: Prepare Fast Green dye solutions
steps.instruction: Make a 10 % Fast Green stock by adding 0.1 g Fast Green to 0.9 mL sterile water for injection in a sterile 1.5 mL microtube, vortex, then dilute 1:10 to obtain a 1 % working solution (100 µL stock + 0.9 mL water). Filter the 1 % solution through a 0.22 µm syringe filter into a new sterile microtube; this filtered 1 % solution will be used for virus visualization.

steps.title: Mix virus with Fast Green for injection
steps.instruction: In a 0.5 mL microtube add 20 µL AAV6‑hSyn‑ChR2(H134R)‑EYFP virus and 2 µL filtered 1 % Fast Green, vortex, briefly centrifuge to collect liquid, and keep on ice (4 °C) for up to 8 h; prepare this mixture on the day of surgery.

steps.title: Set up surgical workspace and warming pad
steps.instruction: Clean the magnetic optical table, place a sterile drape on a warming pad set to 37 °C, sterilize all surgical tools and arrange them on the sterile surface.

steps.title: Prepare syringe and load virus solution
steps.instruction: Attach a 30 G hypodermic needle electrode to a 50 µL microsyringe, draw 22 µL of the virus‑Fast Green mixture into the syringe, and depress the plunger until solution is visible at the tip to confirm no air bubbles.

steps.title: Configure syringe pump and micropositioner
steps.instruction: Connect the syringe pump to its controller, select the 50 µL (60 mm) syringe setting, program an injection of 22 000 nL at 5 µL / min, and attach the loaded syringe to the pump. Then mount the pump on a magnetic micropositioner and move it aside of the surgical field.

steps.title: Anesthetize animal and position for surgery
steps.instruction: Place the rat in an induction box, deliver 3 % isoflurane in room air at 500 mL / min until toe‑pinch reflex is absent, then transfer to a nose‑cone mask with 1.5–2 % isoflurane at 350 mL / min. Position the animal on a disposable pad on its right side.

steps.title: Administer analgesia and prep surgical site
steps.instruction: Apply lubricant eye ointment, inject meloxicam subcutaneously (1–2 mg / kg) and lactated Ringer’s solution (10 mL / kg) for fluid maintenance, place a support under the left leg so the tibia is parallel to the table and tape the ankle, then scrub the lateral left‑leg skin three times with povidone‑iodine followed by 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Make incision and expose tibialis anterior muscle
steps.instruction: Using a scalpel, make a 3–5 mm incision 2–3 mm lateral to the tibia and ~5 mm distal to the knee joint, then blunt‑dissect through skin and fascia to expose the left tibialis anterior (TA) muscle.

steps.title: Place ground electrode subcutaneously
steps.instruction: Insert a disposable subdermal needle electrode under the skin of the left leg about 1–2 cm away from the TA incision; this electrode will serve as the ground for electrical stimulation.

steps.title: Position injection needle using micropositioner
steps.instruction: Mount the syringe on the micropositioner, align the needle to enter the muscle at the proximal end (≈¼ of the distance knee‑to‑ankle), run parallel to TA fibers, and insert at a 30° angle relative to the muscle surface, aiming toward the distal end.

steps.title: Apply electrical stimulation to locate NMJ zone
steps.instruction: Connect the syringe needle to the stimulation channel of an electrical stimulator and the ground electrode to the ground channel; set monopolar biphasic waveform, 0.2 ms pulse width, 1 Hz frequency, and increase current until small twitches appear (typically 75–300 µA). Adjust needle position to maximize twitches, targeting dense NMJ zones distal to the knee (≈⅓–½ of the knee‑to‑ankle distance). Turn off stimulation.

steps.title: Inject virus into tibialis anterior muscle
steps.instruction: Activate the microinjection pump to deliver 22 µL of virus at 5 µL / min as a continuous injection; after each 5 µL, retract the needle slightly to prevent back‑flow. After the injection, wait ≥2 min for dispersion, then slowly withdraw the needle and remove the ground electrode. The Fast Green dye will visibly mark the TA muscle.

steps.title: Close incision and recover animal
steps.instruction: Suture the skin with 4‑0 to 5‑0 suture material, remove the animal from anesthesia, return it to its home cage, monitor until fully awake, and administer postoperative meloxicam (1–2 mg / kg SC) once daily for three days.

steps.title: Set up EMG recording equipment
steps.instruction: Power on the electrophysiology system, connect subdermal EMG electrodes for differential recording, set headstage gain to 1, enable AC coupling, and sample at ~12.2 kHz to capture spike waveforms.

steps.title: Prepare laser and calibrate light output
steps.instruction: Connect a 200 µm, 0.22 NA optical fiber to a 470 nm laser, mount the fiber on a probe holder attached to a micropositioner, position the fiber tip 2–3 mm above a calibrated power sensor, turn on the laser at maximum power, record the maximum output, then set the intensity to the minimum planned experimental value and record that as well.

steps.title: Anesthetize animal for transdermal assessment
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with 3 % isoflurane (500 mL / min) until toe‑pinch reflex is absent, then maintain with 1.5–2 % isoflurane (350 mL / min) via nose cone; place the animal on its right side on a warming pad and remove hair from the lateral left leg.

steps.title: Insert EMG needle electrodes into tibialis anterior
steps.instruction: Insert two disposable subdermal needle electrodes ~2 mm apart along the long axis of the TA muscle at ~45° to the skin so the full 7 mm electrode length lies within the muscle, and connect them to the recording system.

steps.title: Insert ground needle and position laser over peroneal nerve
steps.instruction: Place a metal‑hub hypodermic needle subcutaneously in the animal’s back, attach an alligator clip as ground, then move the laser‑mounted micropositioner to a point 0–1 mm above the leg over the peroneal nerve (lateral to TA, ≈⅓ of the distance knee‑to‑ankle).

steps.title: Perform laser scanning to locate optimal stimulation site
steps.instruction: Activate pulsed laser stimulation (1 Hz, 5 ms pulse width, maximum intensity) and, while delivering pulses, slowly scan the laser across the leg; monitor EMG and adjust laser position until the peak‑to‑peak EMG amplitude is maximal, indicating alignment with the peroneal nerve.

steps.title: Execute optical stimulation sequences
steps.instruction:
Run three parameter sweeps:
 a) Light‑intensity sweep: 20–240 mW (10–15 steps), 5 ms pulse, 1 Hz, 10 pulses per train.
 b) Pulse‑width sweep: 0.5–10 ms (10 steps) at 240 mW, 0.5 Hz, 10 pulses per train.
 c) Frequency sweep: 1–75 Hz (multiple values) at 240 mW, 5 ms pulse, 2 s train duration; insert ≥5 s pause between trains.

steps.title: Remove electrodes, recover animal, and analyze EMG data
steps.instruction: Detach EMG and ground needles, discontinue anesthesia, monitor the rat until fully awake, then compute response magnitudes as RMS of the EMG signal over a 15 ms window starting at each optical pulse onset, average over 5–10 trials, and consider a response valid if spikes occur on ≥75 % of pulses and peak amplitude ≥4× the noise RMS.

steps.title: Euthanize and perfuse animal transcardially
steps.instruction: Inject pentobarbital (150–200 mg / kg IP) and confirm loss of corneal and toe‑pinch reflexes, open the chest by cutting ribs to create a flap, insert a blunt 20 G needle into the left ventricle directed toward the aorta and secure with hemostats, cut the right atrium for outflow, then perfuse with 200 mL cold 1× PBS at ~80 mL / min followed by 200 mL cold 4 % PFA in PBS.

steps.title: Dissect peroneal nerve, TA muscle, and spinal cord
steps.instruction:
Harvest the left TA muscle, peroneal nerve, and spinal cord:
 • For nerve: make a large lateral leg incision, blunt‑dissect skin, TA and biceps femoris (BF), incise fascia to expose peroneal nerve, follow it proximally, detach BF at knee, cut sciatic proximally, cut TA tendon distally, remove TA and accessory muscles while preserving the nerve.
 • For spinal cord: make a dorsal skin incision from head to pelvis, cut laterally along the vertebrae from L6 rostrally to at least mid‑thoracic, cut the column rostrally and caudally, then post‑fix the spinal column in 4 % PFA overnight.

steps.title: Post‑fix tissues and store for later processing
steps.instruction: Place spinal cord samples in 4 % PFA at 4 °C overnight; keep nerve samples in 4 % PFA for 15 min. After fixation, transfer all samples to 1× PBS containing 0.02 % sodium azide and store at 4 °C. Freeze samples within 4–6 weeks for optimal imaging.

steps.title: Cryoprotect, embed, and section tissues for IHC
steps.instruction: Incubate dissected nerve or spinal cord pieces in 20 % sucrose in PBS overnight at 4 °C, embed in OCT compound, freeze rapidly with liquid nitrogen or equivalent, and cut 14–30 µm cross‑sections on a cryostat.

steps.title: Perform immunohistochemistry staining on sections
steps.instruction:
Wash sections in PBS 5 min ×3. Optional amplification:
 1) Block 30 min at RT in 1 % normal donkey serum + 1 % Triton X‑100 in PBS.
 2) Wash PBS 5 min ×3.
 3) Incubate with rabbit anti‑GFP (1:200) overnight at 4 °C in the same buffer.
 4) Wash PBS 5 min ×3.
 5) Incubate with donkey anti‑rabbit AF647 (1:100) for 2 h at RT.
 6) Wash PBS 5 min ×3.
 Then mount coverslips with ProLong Diamond antifade medium.

steps.title: Mount slides and image with confocal microscope
steps.instruction: Place the stained slides on a microscope stage, select appropriate laser lines and detector settings for the fluorophore (e.g., EYFP or AF647), acquire confocal images of the peroneal nerve or spinal cord to visualize opsin expression.
